readings.title: The Death of Ezekiel's Wife
readings.subtitle: A Sign of the Temple's Destruction
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 24:15] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[16] <dq>“Son of man, see, <dn>I</dn> am taking away from you <dn>את</dn> the desire of your eyes with one stroke. But do not mourn, nor weep, nor let your tears run down.</dq>
[17] <dq>“Groan silently, make no mourning for the dead. Bind your turban on your head, and put your sandals on your feet. Do not cover your upper lip, and do not eat man’s bread of sorrow.”</dq>
[18] And <dn>I</dn> spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died. And the next morning <dn>I</dn> did as <dn>I</dn> was commanded.
[19] And the people said to me, “Would you not explain to us what these matters you are doing mean to us?”
[20] And <dn>I</dn> said to them, “The word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[21] Speak to the house of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am profaning <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> set-apart place – the pride of your strength, the desire of your eyes, and the delight of your being. And your sons and daughters whom you left behind shall fall by the sword.</dq>
[22] <dq>And you shall do as <dn>I</dn> have done, do not cover your upper lip nor eat man’s bread of sorrow,</dq>
[23] <dq>and let your turbans remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet. Do not mourn, nor weep, but you shall pine away in your crookednesses and groan with one another.</dq>
[24] <dq>And Yeḥezqěl shall be a sign to you. Do according to all that he has done. When this comes, you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>
[25] <dq>And you, son of man, on the day when <dn>I</dn> take from them <dn>את</dn> their stronghold, <dn>את</dn> the joy of their adorning, <dn>את</dn> the desire of their eyes, and <dn>את</dn> the lifting up of their being, <dn>את</dn> their sons and <dn>את</dn> their daughters,</dq>
[26] <dq>on that day one that has escaped shall come to you to let you hear it with your ears.</dq>
[27] <dq>On that day your mouth shall be opened to him who has escaped, and you shall speak and no longer be silent. And you shall be a sign to them. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Prophecy Against Ammon
readings.subtitle: For Rejoicing Over Judah's Fall
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 25:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] “Son of man, set your face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them.
[3] “And you shall say to the Ammonites, ‘Hear the word of the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Because you said, ‘Aha!’ against <dn>My</dn> set-apart place when it was profaned, and against the land of Yisra’ěl when it was ruined, and against the house of Yehuḏah when they went into exile,</dq>
[4] <dq>therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am giving you as a possession to the men of the East, and they shall set their encampments among you and make their dwellings among you – they shall eat your fruit, and they shall drink your milk.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make Rabbah a pasture for camels and Ammon a resting place for flocks. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>
[6] For this is what the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Because you clapped your hands, and you stamped your feet, and rejoiced with all the scorn of your being against the land of Yisra’ěl,</dq>
[7] <dq>therefore see, <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall stretch out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand against you, and give you as plunder to the nations. And <dn>I</dn> shall cut you off from the peoples, and make you perish from the lands. <dn>I</dn> shall destroy you, and you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: Prophecy Against Moab and Seir
readings.subtitle: For Likening Judah to Other Nations
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 25:8] This is what the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Because Mo’aḇ and Sě‛ir say, ‘See, the house of Yehuḏah is like all the nations,’</dq>
[9] <dq>therefore, see, <dn>I</dn> am opening <dn>את</dn> the flank of Mo’aḇ on the side of the cities, on the side of his cities on its frontiers, the splendour of the land, Běyth Yeshimoth, Ba‛al Me‛on, and Qiryathayim,</dq>
[10] <dq>and <dn>I</dn> shall give it, together with the Ammonites, as a possession to the men of the East, so that the Ammonites are no more remembered among the nations.</dq>
[11] <dq>“Also on Mo’aḇ <dn>I</dn> execute judgments, and they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: Prophecy Against Edom
readings.subtitle: For Taking Vengeance on Judah
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 25:12] Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Because of what Eḏom has done against the house of Yehuḏah by taking vengeance, so that they became very guilty, and they have taken vengeance on them,”</dq>
[13] <dq>therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “<dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand against Eḏom, and <dn>I</dn> shall cut off man and beast from it and lay it waste – from Těman even to Deḏan they shall fall by the sword.</dq>
[14] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall lay <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> vengeance on Eḏom by the hand of <dn>My</dn> people Yisra’ěl. And they shall do in Eḏom according to <dn>My</dn> displeasure and according to <dn>My</dn> wrath. So they shall know <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> vengeance,” declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>

readings.title: Prophecy Against the Philistines
readings.subtitle: For Acting in Vengeance
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 25:15] Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Because the Philistines have acted in vengeance, and took vengeance with scorn in their being, to destroy with lasting enmity,”</dq>
[16] <dq>therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, <dn>I</dn> am stretching out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand against the Philistines, and <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> the Kerěthites and destroy <dn>את</dn> the remnant of the seacoast,</dq>
[17] <dq>and execute great vengeance on them with raging reproofs. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> lay <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> vengeance upon them.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: A Message for King Zedekiah
readings.subtitle: Prophecy of Captivity and a Peaceful Death
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 34:1] The word which came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar sovereign of Baḇel and all his army, and all the reigns of the earth under his rule, and all the people, fought against Yerushalayim and all its cities, saying,
[2] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘Go and speak to Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah and say to him, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> this city into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel. And he shall burn it with fire,</dq>
[3] <dq>and you shall not escape out of his hand, but certainly be taken and given into his hand. And your eyes shall see <dn>את</dn> the eyes of the sovereign of Baḇel, and his mouth shall speak with your mouth, and you shall go to Baḇel.’ ” ’</dq>
[4] <dq>“But hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah! Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> concerning you, ‘You shall not die by the sword.</dq>
[5] <dq>In peace you are to die, and as in the burnings of spices for your fathers, the former sovereigns who were before you, so they shall burn spices for you and lament for you, saying, “Alas, master!” ’ For <dn>I</dn> have spoken <dn>את</dn> the word,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq>
[6] And Yirmeyahu the prophet spoke <dn>את</dn> all these words to Tsiḏqiyahu the sovereign of Yehuḏah in Yerushalayim,
[7] while the sovereign of Baḇel’s army was fighting against Yerushalayim and all the cities of Yehuḏah that were left, against Laḵish and Azěqah. For only these walled cities remained of the cities of Yehuḏah.

readings.title: The Broken Covenant of Freedom
readings.subtitle: Judah Re-enslaves Their Brothers
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 34:8] The word which came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, after Sovereign Tsiḏqiyahu had made <dn>את</dn> a covenant with all the people who were at Yerushalayim to proclaim release to them:
[9] that everyone was to set free <dn>את</dn> his male and <dn>את</dn> female slave, the Hebrew man and the Hebrew woman, no one was to keep a Yehuḏi, his brother, enslaved.
[10] And when all the heads and all the people who had come into the covenant heard that each one was to set free his male and female slaves, and not keep them enslaved any longer, they obeyed and released them.
[11] But afterward they changed their minds and made the male and female slaves return, whom they had set free, and brought them into subjection as male and female slaves.
[12] Therefore the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying,
[13] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> made <dn>את</dn> a covenant with <dn>את</dn> your fathers in the day that <dn>I</dn> brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, out of the house of bondage, saying,</dq>
[14] <dq>“At the end of seven years each one should set free <dn>את</dn> his Hebrew brother, who has been sold to him. And when he has served you six years, you shall let him go free from you.” But your fathers did not obey <dn>Me</dn> nor incline their ear.</dq>
[15] <dq>And you recently turned and did <dn>את</dn> what was right in <dn>My</dn> eyes, each man proclaiming release to his neighbour. And you made <dn>את</dn> a covenant before <dn>Me</dn> in the house which is called by <dn>My</dn> Name.</dq>
[16] <dq>But you turned back and profaned <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> Name, and each one of you took back <dn>את</dn> his male and <dn>את</dn> female slaves, whom he had set free, at their pleasure, and brought them into subjection, to be your male and female slaves.’</dq>
[17] <dq>“Therefore thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘You have not obeyed <dn>Me</dn> in proclaiming release, each one to his brother and each one to his neighbour. See, <dn>I</dn> am proclaiming release to you,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the scarcity of food! And <dn>I</dn> shall make you a horror to all reigns of the earth.</dq>
[18] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> the men who are transgressing <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> covenant, who have not established <dn>את</dn> the words of the covenant which they made before <dn>Me</dn>, when they cut <dn>את</dn> the calf in two and passed between the parts of it:</dq>
[19] <dq>the heads of Yehuḏah, and <dn>את</dn> the heads of Yerushalayim, <dn>את</dn> the eunuchs, and <dn>את</dn> the priests, and <dn>את</dn> all the people of the land who passed between the parts of the calf.</dq>
[20] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their life. And their corpses shall be for food to the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth.</dq>
[21] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah and <dn>את</dn> his heads into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those who seek their life, and into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel’s army that has withdrawn from you.</dq>
[22] <dq>See, <dn>I</dn> am commanding,’ declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ’and shall bring them back to this city, and they shall fight against it and take it and burn it with fire. And <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> the cities of Yehuḏah a ruin without inhabitant.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Zedekiah's Desperate Inquiry
readings.subtitle: The Way of Life and the Way of Death
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 21:1] The word that came to Yirmeyahu from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> when Sovereign Tsiḏqiyahu sent to him Pashḥur son of Malkiyah, and Tsephanyah the son of Ma‛asěyah, the priest, saying,
[2] “Please inquire of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on our behalf, for Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel has started fighting against us. It might be that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> deals with us according to all <dn>His</dn> wondrous works, so that he withdraws from us.”
[3] But Yirmeyahu said to them, “Say this to Tsiḏqiyahu,
[4] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am turning back <dn>את</dn> the weapons of battle that are in your hands, with which you fight against the sovereign of Baḇel and the Kasdim who besiege you outside the wall. And <dn>I</dn> shall gather them inside this city.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> <dn>Myself</dn> shall fight against you with an outstretched hand, and with a strong arm, even in displeasure and rage and great wrath.</dq>
[6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall strike <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of this city, both <dn>את</dn> man and <dn>את</dn> beast – let them die of a great pestilence.</dq>
[7] <dq>“And afterward,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “<dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> Tsiḏqiyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, <dn>את</dn> his servants and <dn>את</dn> the people, and <dn>את</dn> such as are left in this city from the pestilence and the sword and the scarcity of food, into the hand of Neḇuḵaḏretstsar sovereign of Baḇel, into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of those who seek their life. And he shall strike them with the edge of the sword. He shall not pardon them, nor spare nor have compassion.” ’</dq>
[8] <dq>“You shall also say to this people, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, <dn>I</dn> set before you <dn>את</dn> the way of life and <dn>את</dn> the way of death.</dq>
[9] <dq>“Whoever stays in this city dies by the sword, by scarcity of food, and by pestilence. But whoever goes out and shall go over to the Kasdim who besiege you, is going to live, and his life shall be as a prize to him.</dq>
[10] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have set <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> face against this city for evil and not for good,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. “It is given into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel, and he shall burn it with fire.” ’</dq>

readings.title: A Word to the House of David
readings.subtitle: A Call for Justice
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 21:11] “And to the house of the sovereign of Yehuḏah, say, ‘Hear <dn>את</dn> the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,
[12] O house of Daviḏ! Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Render right-ruling in the morning, and deliver him who has been robbed out of the hand of the oppressor, lest <dn>My</dn> wrath go out like fire and burn, with no one to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds.</dq>
[13] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against you, O inhabitant of the valley, rock of the plain,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “who are saying, ‘Who would come down against us? And who would come into our dwellings?’</dq>
[14] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall punish you according to the fruit of your deeds,” declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. “And <dn>I</dn> shall kindle a fire in its forest, and it shall consume <dn>את</dn> all that is around her.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Pharaoh, the Great Monster
readings.subtitle: Egypt to be Desolate for Forty Years
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 29:1] In the tenth year, in the tenth month, on the twelfth of the new moon, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] “Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh the sovereign of Mitsrayim, and prophesy against him, and against Mitsrayim, all of it.
[3] “Speak, and you shall say, ‘Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am against you, O Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, O great monster who lies in the midst of his rivers, who has said, ‘<dn>My</dn> River is my own, and <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have made it for <dn>myself</dn>.’</dq>
[4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall put hooks in your jaws, and <dn>I</dn> shall make the fish of your rivers cling to your scales. And <dn>I</dn> shall bring you up out of the midst of your rivers, and all the fish in your rivers cling to your scales.</dq>
[5] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall leave you in the wilderness, <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> all the fish of your rivers. On the face of the field you shall fall, and you shall not be picked up or gathered. <dn>I</dn> shall give you as food to the beasts of the field and to the birds of the heavens.</dq>
[6] <dq>“And all the inhabitants of Mitsrayim shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because they have been a staff of reed to the house of Yisra’ěl.</dq>
[7] <dq>“When they grasped you with the hand, you broke and tore all their shoulders. When they leaned on you, you broke and made all their loins shake.”</dq>
[8] <dq>Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing a sword upon you and shall cut off from you man and beast.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And the land of Mitsrayim shall become a desert and a waste. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because he said, ‘The River is mine, and <dn>I</dn> have made it.’</dq>
[10] <dq>“Therefore see, <dn>I</dn> am against you and against your rivers, and shall make <dn>את</dn> the land of Mitsrayim an utter waste and a desert, from Miḡdol to Sewěněh, as far as the border of Kush.</dq>
[11] <dq>“No foot of man shall pass through it, nor foot of beast pass through it, neither shall it be inhabited for forty years.</dq>
[12] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> the land of Mitsrayim a desert in the midst of the lands that are waste. And among the cities that are ruined, her cities shall be a waste forty years. And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites among the nations, and <dn>I</dn> shall disperse them throughout the lands.”</dq>
[13] <dq>For thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “At the end of forty years <dn>I</dn> shall gather <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites from the peoples among whom they were scattered.</dq>
[14] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall turn back <dn>את</dn> the captivity of Mitsrayim and <dn>I</dn> shall bring them back to the land of Pathros, to the land of their birth, and there they shall be a lowly reign,</dq>
[15] <dq>being the lowliest of reigns, and never again exalt itself above the nations. And <dn>I</dn> shall make them few so as not to rule over the nations.</dq>
[16] <dq>“And no longer is it to be the refuge of the house of Yisra’ěl, bringing to remembrance their crookedness when they turned to follow them. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” ’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Pharaoh's Broken Arm
readings.subtitle: The King of Babylon's Arms Strengthened
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 30:20] And it came to be in the eleventh year, in the first month, on the seventh of the new moon, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[21] <dq>“Son of man, <dn>I</dn> have broken <dn>את</dn> the arm of Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim. And see, it has not been bound up for healing, to put a bandage to bind it, to make it strong to hold a sword.</dq>
[22] <dq>“Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am against Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, and shall break <dn>את</dn> his arms, both <dn>את</dn> the strong one and <dn>את</dn> the one that was broken, and shall make <dn>את</dn> the sword fall out of his hand,</dq>
[23] <dq>and shall scatter <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites among the nations, and disperse them throughout the lands,</dq>
[24] <dq>and strengthen <dn>את</dn> the arms of the sovereign of Baḇel. And <dn>I</dn> shall put <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> sword in his hand. And <dn>I</dn> shall break <dn>את</dn> Pharaoh’s arms, and he shall groan before him with the groanings of the slain before him.</dq>
[25] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall strengthen <dn>את</dn> the arms of the sovereign of Baḇel, but the arms of Pharaoh shall fall. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> put <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> sword into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel and he shall stretch it out against the land of Mitsrayim.</dq>
[26] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall scatter <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites among the nations, and <dn>I</dn> shall disperse them throughout the lands. And they shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Great Cedar of Lebanon
readings.subtitle: A Parable of Assyria's Fall as a Warning to Pharaoh
readings.text:
[Ezekiel 31:1] And it came to be in the eleventh year, in the third month, on the first of the new moon, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] “Son of man, say to Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim and to his crowd, <dq>‘To whom are you to be compared in your greatness?</dq>
[3] <dq>See, Ashshur was a cedar in Leḇanon, beautiful branches and forest shade, and of high stature. And its top was among the thick foliage.</dq>
[4] <dq>The waters made him great, the deep gave it height with its rivers running around its planting, and sent <dn>את</dn> their channels to all the trees of the field.</dq>
[5] <dq>Therefore its height was lifted up above all the trees of the field, and its boughs were increased, and its branches became long because of the many waters, as it sent them out.</dq>
[6] <dq>All the birds of the heavens made their nests in its boughs, and under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth. And in its shadow all great nations dwelt.</dq>
[7] <dq>And it was beautiful in greatness and in the length of its branches, for its roots reached to many waters.</dq>
[8] <dq>Cedars in the garden of <dn>Elohim</dn> did not hide it, fir trees were not like its boughs, and the chestnut trees were not like its branches. No tree in the garden of <dn>Elohim</dn> was as pretty as it.</dq>
[9] <dq><dn>I</dn> made it beautiful by its many branches, so that all the trees of Ěḏen which were in the garden of <dn>Elohim</dn> were jealous of it.’</dq>
[10] <dq>“Therefore thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘Because you have increased in height, and it set <dn>את</dn> its top among the thick foliage, and its heart was lifted up in its height,</dq>
[11] <dq><dn>I</dn> give it into the hand of the mighty one of the nations, and he shall certainly deal with it. <dn>I</dn> have driven it out for its wrong.</dq>
[12] <dq>And foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations, shall cut it down and leave it. Its branches shall fall on the mountains and in all the valleys, its boughs lie broken by all the rivers of the land. And all the peoples of the earth shall come out from under its shadow and leave it.</dq>
[13] <dq>On its ruin shall dwell all the birds of the heavens, and all the beasts of the field shall be on its fallen branches,</dq>
[14] <dq>so that none of the trees by the waters would exalt themselves because of their height, nor set <dn>את</dn> their tops among the thick foliage, and that no tree which drinks water would ever be high enough to reach up to them. ‘For all of them shall be given up to death, to the depths of the earth, among the children of men who go down to the pit.’</dq>
[15] <dq>“Thus said the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, ‘In the day when it is brought down to She’ol <dn>I</dn> shall cause mourning. <dn>I</dn> shall cover <dn>את</dn> the deep because of it and hold back its streams, and many waters shall be confined. And <dn>I</dn> shall make Leḇanon mourn for it, and all the trees of the field shall wither away because of it.</dq>
[16] <dq><dn>I</dn> shall make the nations shake at the sound of its fall, when <dn>I</dn> bring it down to She’ol together with those who descend into the pit. And all the trees of Ěḏen, the choice and best of Leḇanon, all that drink water, shall be comforted in the depths of the earth.</dq>
[17] <dq>They too shall go down to She’ol with it, with those slain by the sword. And those who were its strength shall dwell in its shadows among the nations.</dq>
[18] <dq>To whom are you to be compared in esteem and greatness among the trees in Ěḏen? But you shall be brought down with <dn>את</dn> the trees of Ěḏen to the depths of the earth, lie in the midst of the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his crowd,’ declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq>
